testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What is a problem with driving a trailer that carries hanging meat?

options.text: It should not be done in summer.
Animals may be attracted to the smell.
The load is unstable because it sits high and can swing.

questions.correctAnswerText: The load is unstable because it sits high and can swing.
questions.explanation: Hanging meat creates an unstable load. It has a high center of gravity and swings as you drive, which makes the vehicle harder to control.

questions.question: What should you do before transporting an oversized load?

options.text: You cannot transport oversized loads.
Only transport them during daylight hours.
Get special permits to follow state and local laws.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get special permits to follow state and local laws.
questions.explanation: You need special permits before transporting loads that are too large, too long, or too heavy.

questions.question: When should you shift to a lower gear before going downhill?

options.text: Before you start going downhill.
After you have started going downhill.
As far down the hill as possible.

questions.explanation: Shift to a lower gear before you begin driving downhill. Gravity will make your vehicle speed up, so you need to be prepared.

questions.question: If a tire fails while you are driving, what should you do?

options.text: Use the brakes hard.
Do not use the brakes.
Swerve to avoid obstacles.
Wave your arms to warn other drivers.

questions.explanation: Using the brakes after a tire fails can cause you to lose control. Unless you are about to hit something, avoid braking until your vehicle has slowed down on its own.

questions.question: What should a driver do if they feel tired while driving?

options.text: Keep driving.
Drink coffee.
Stop and sleep.
Drive faster to finish sooner.

questions.explanation: The only safe action when you feel drowsy is to pull over and rest. Caffeine and stimulants are not safe because they can wear off suddenly and make you even more tired.

questions.question: What happens when cargo has a high center of gravity?

options.text: The vehicle is more likely to tip over.
It is safe to use in bad weather.
It is required on some roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle is more likely to tip over.
questions.explanation: Cargo with a high center of gravity makes a vehicle more likely to tip. Always keep the weight of cargo as low as possible.

questions.question: What kind of load does hanging meat create?

options.text: A safe load.
An unstable load.
A load that should never be transported.
A load with a low center of gravity.

questions.explanation: Hanging meat is unstable. The truck becomes top-heavy and the swinging meat affects steering. Be extra careful on curves and highway ramps.

questions.question: Overloading cargo harms all of the following except:

options.text: Steering.
Braking.
Speed control.
The electrical system.

questions.explanation: Overloading hurts steering, braking, and speed control. Pay attention to how your vehicle handles when it is heavier.

questions.question: What does ABS do?

options.text: Stop wheels from locking up.
Stop the air compressor from overheating.
Stop front brakes from working on ice.
Stop brakes from being used if downshifting works better.

questions.explanation: ABS (Anti-Lock Braking System) prevents wheels from locking up when you brake hard, especially on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: When should you check cargo to make sure it is secure?

options.text: Only before you start the trip.
Before you start and again within the first 50 miles.
Only the loading crew needs to check it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start and again within the first 50 miles.
questions.explanation: Check cargo before the trip starts and again within the first 50 miles. Then check it every three hours or every 150 miles. Check it every time you stop for a break. You are responsible for keeping cargo safe the entire trip.

questions.question: A tired driver:

options.text: Is very alert.
Should take over-the-counter pills to stay awake.
May make important decisions too slowly.
Is usually more careful than other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: May make important decisions too slowly.
questions.explanation: When tired, you will not see hazards or react to them as quickly as when you are fully awake. You will have trouble making important decisions.

questions.question: If a reckless driver crashes on the road ahead of you, you should:

options.text: Block the driver in with your vehicle.
Stop a safe distance away and tell police about the driver's reckless behavior.
Keep driving and ignore it.
Pull over and yell at the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop a safe distance away and tell police about the driver's reckless behavior.
questions.explanation: If you see a crash with a reckless driver, stop at a safe distance from the crash. Wait for police to arrive and tell them what you saw about the reckless driving.

questions.question: On newer vehicles, how do you set the parking brake?

options.text: Move a lever to the right.
Push in the yellow diamond-shaped knob.
Pull out the yellow diamond-shaped knob.
Pull up on the steering column.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull out the yellow diamond-shaped knob.
questions.explanation: On newer vehicles with air brakes, the parking brake has a yellow diamond-shaped knob. Pull the knob out to set the brakes. Push it in to release them.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi in:

options.text: Two minutes.
15 seconds.
10 minutes.
45 seconds.

questions.explanation: When checking a dual air brake system, wait for air pressure to build from 85 to 100 psi in both systems. This should take about 45 seconds.

questions.question: If your brakes fail going downhill, the best way to stop is to:

options.text: Use an escape ramp.
Use the shoulder.
Drift to a stop.

questions.explanation: If your brakes fail going downhill, look for an escape ramp. It is the safest way to stop your vehicle.

questions.question: When starting a vehicle with dual air brakes, pressure of ____ must build up before driving.

options.text: 10 psi
25 psi
100 psi
200 psi

questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, let the air compressor build up at least 100 psi of pressure in both systems.

questions.question: States check that a CDL or CLP driver has only one license by:

options.text: Calling other states.
Using a computer system that connects all states.
Asking the driver.
Looking through the driver's wallet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using a computer system that connects all states.
questions.explanation: All U.S. states share CDL and CLP information in a computer database. When you apply for a license in one state, they check this database to make sure you do not already have one in another state.

questions.question: Distracted driving:

options.text: Can be avoided by eating while driving.
Can be increased by pre-programming radio stations.
Can be avoided by not having complex conversations while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be avoided by not having complex conversations while driving.
questions.explanation: Distractions can be physical (reaching for something), mental (talking with a passenger), or both (texting on a phone). To avoid distracted driving: pre-program radio stations, plan your route ahead of time, avoid difficult or emotional conversations, adjust mirrors before you leave, and do not eat, drink, or smoke while driving.

questions.question: An air compressor governor controls:

options.text: When air is pumped into the air storage tanks.
How fast air is pumped into the air storage tanks.
The temperature of air going into the air storage tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: When air is pumped into the air storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when air is pumped into the air storage tanks in an air brake system.

questions.question: Air tank drains:

options.text: Should not be used in cold weather.
Help remove water and oil from the air tanks.
Are used to send air to the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help remove water and oil from the air tanks.
questions.explanation: Compressed air in an air brake system usually contains water and oil. These can damage the system if they build up. Air tanks have drain valves to remove water and oil from the air.

questions.question: When driving on the expressway during the skills test, you should:

options.text: Switch lanes frequently.
Use your mirrors to check traffic as needed.
Drive on the left side of the lane.
Drive above the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your mirrors to check traffic as needed.
questions.explanation: On the expressway, keep your lane position steady and maintain safe distance from other vehicles. Drive at the posted speed limit. Check your mirrors often to see traffic around you in all directions.

questions.question: Pressing and releasing the brake pedal unnecessarily can:

options.text: Release air faster than it can be replaced.
Add more air to a brake system.
Make the brake pedal harder to depress.
Create a loud noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release air faster than it can be replaced.
questions.explanation: Vehicles with air brakes lose air when you press and release the brake pedal too much. The air compressor may not be able to replace the air fast enough. This can cause the air pressure to drop too low, and the brakes may fail.

questions.question: The suspension system:

options.text: Holds up the vehicle and its load.
Keeps the load the proper distance behind the driver's compartment.
Maintains a safe distance between the vehicle and other vehicles.
Lightens the load for the tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Holds up the vehicle and its load.
questions.explanation: The suspension system supports the vehicle and its load while keeping the axles in place. Damage to the suspension system is very dangerous.

questions.question: If mirrors are dirty before starting a trip:

options.text: They will likely become clean after driving a short distance.
It should not be a concern.
They should be cleaned before the vehicle is driven.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should be cleaned before the vehicle is driven.
questions.explanation: Before you start driving, check your mirrors and windshield. Clean them if they are dirty or have anything blocking your view.

questions.question: If a tire rim is damaged, it should be:

options.text: Left on the vehicle.
Welded to repair the damage.
Replaced.
Put on the axle farthest from the driver.

questions.explanation: Do not weld damaged wheels or rims. They are not safe. Replace the damaged rim instead.

questions.question: If convicted of a traffic violation, you must inform your employer:

options.text: Within three hours.
Within a week.
Within 30 days.

questions.explanation: You must tell your employer within 30 days of any traffic conviction, no matter what vehicle you were driving. You must also notify your motor vehicle licensing agency within 30 days if the violation happened in another state. Parking tickets do not count.

questions.question: If you are driving and the ABS light comes on, it means that the ABS:

options.text: Cannot work due to weather conditions.
Has just been activated.
Is not working properly.

questions.explanation: When the ABS warning light comes on, there is a problem with the Anti-Lock Braking System.

questions.question: When exiting a vehicle, a driver should:

options.text: Hop directly from their seat to the ground.
Maintain at least one point of contact with their vehicle.
Be turned to face their vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be turned to face their vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you exit your vehicle during the skills test, face the vehicle and hold on with three points of contact. For a bus, hold the handrail. Not exiting correctly may cause you to fail the basic vehicle control skills test.

questions.question: What happens if brakes become too hot?

options.text: They will become too smooth.
They will harden.
They may stop working.
The air compressor will kick in to cool the brakes.

questions.explanation: If you use the brakes too much, they can overheat and stop working. This is called brake fade.

questions.question: To receive a hazardous materials endorsement, an applicant will be required to supply:

options.text: Their fingerprints.
Their shoe size.
A list of countries visited within the last 10 years.
Their employment history for the previous five years.

questions.explanation: To get a hazardous materials endorsement, you must submit your fingerprints and pass a TSA background check.

questions.question: A 40-foot load needs how many tie-downs at minimum?

options.text: Two tie-downs.
Three tie-downs.
Four tie-downs.

questions.explanation: On flatbed trailers, use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. Always use at least two tie-downs, no matter the cargo size.

questions.question: When backing with a trailer, why should you turn toward the driver's side?

options.text: Because it allows the driver a better view.
Because turning toward the passenger side is illegal.
Because other drivers can offer assistance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Because it allows the driver a better view.
questions.explanation: Back toward the driver's side when possible. This gives you the best view of your path.

questions.question: What does poor weight balance do?

options.text: Improves a vehicle's handling.
Makes handling a vehicle more difficult.
Increases a driver's ability to steer.
Makes a vehicle easier to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes handling a vehicle more difficult.
questions.explanation: Poor weight balance makes a vehicle harder and less safe to handle.

questions.question: You are convicted of a traffic violation in your personal car. What must you do?

options.text: The convicting officer will alert your employer.
Your CDL will not be affected because the violation is on your personal license.
You should tell your employer within six months.
You must tell your employer within 30 days.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must tell your employer within 30 days.
questions.explanation: You must notify your employer within 30 days of any traffic conviction in any vehicle. Parking violations do not count.

questions.question: Which action best helps avoid a crash?

options.text: Braking is always the best option.
Swerving may be more effective than braking.
Drivers should leave 100 yards of distance between their vehicle and the next.

questions.correctAnswerText: Swerving may be more effective than braking.
questions.explanation: You can turn to avoid an obstacle faster than you can stop. Braking is not always the safest choice.

questions.question: What tread depth is required for tires that are not at the front of a commercial vehicle?

options.text: 1/32 of an inch
2/32 of an inch
4/32 of an inch

questions.explanation: Front tires need 4/32 inch tread depth. All other tires need 2/32 inch tread depth.

questions.question: When making a tight turn, how should you use your mirrors?

options.text: Not use your mirrors, as they can be distracting.
Use your mirrors, but not too frequently.
Use your mirrors frequently.
Rely only on your mirrors.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often during tight maneuvers.

questions.question: If the safety relief valve in an air brake system releases air, what does this mean?

options.text: You should not be concerned as this is a normal process.
There is something wrong with the brakes.
The valve is operational.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is something wrong with the brakes.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air if pressure gets too high. If it releases air, something is wrong. Have a mechanic check it.

questions.question: Before each drive, how should the air compressor drive belt on an air brake vehicle be?

options.text: Loose
Tight
Cracked
Bumpy

questions.explanation: Check the air compressor belt before each drive. It should be tight and in good condition.

questions.question: On a vehicle with power steering, what should you check on the hoses?

options.text: For leaks.
To ensure that they are still clear.
To ensure that they are connected to the battery.
For the proper amount of brake fluid.

questions.explanation: Check power steering hoses, pumps, and fluid level for leaks.

questions.question: After you change a tire and start driving, you should stop after a short distance to:

options.text: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
Check that the tire is wearing evenly.
Check that the tire air pressure is good.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After you change a tire and start driving, stop after a short distance to recheck that the lug nuts are tight.

questions.question: An emergency brake must be controlled by:

options.text: Mechanical force.
Air pressure.
Gravity.

questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have emergency brakes and parking brakes. Air pressure can leak away, so emergency and parking brakes must be held by mechanical force.

questions.question: Most heavy-duty vehicles use ____ air brake systems.

options.text: Single
Dual
Triple
Quad

questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles have dual air brake systems.

questions.question: What is traction?

options.text: Friction between the tires and road
How fast the tires rotate
How long it takes for brakes to work

questions.correctAnswerText: Friction between the tires and road
questions.explanation: Traction is the friction between your tires and the road. You need good traction to brake and steer safely.

questions.question: When driving on wet roads, what does it mean if other vehicles are not spraying water?

options.text: Ice has formed on the road.
The road is dry.
The spray is stuck under the vehicles.
The tires have soaked up the water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ice has formed on the road.
questions.explanation: If the road looks wet but other vehicles' wheels are not spraying water, ice has formed on the road. Drive carefully on wet or icy roads.

questions.question: What information must interstate carriers display on their commercial vehicles?

options.text: Trade name
Width of the truck
Length of the truck

questions.explanation: Federal rules require carriers to display the legal name or trade name on each commercial vehicle in their fleet.

questions.question: If you plan to transport hazardous materials, you must:

options.text: Get a hazardous materials endorsement.
Drive with flashing lights on.
Wear a gas mask.

questions.explanation: You must have a hazardous materials endorsement to transport hazardous materials that require vehicle placards.

questions.question: When using your turn signal, you should:

options.text: Signal before you turn.
Turn off the signal before you turn.
Signal only if vehicles are ahead of you.

questions.explanation: Always signal well before you turn. This tells other drivers your plans and keeps them from trying to pass you. Without a signal, drivers may think you are just slowing down or stopping.

questions.question: Who is responsible for making sure cargo is loaded properly?

options.text: The driver
The shipper
The recipient

questions.explanation: The driver is responsible for inspecting the cargo, checking for overloads and poor weight balance, securing the cargo without blocking their view, and keeping emergency equipment accessible.

questions.question: Hanging meat:

options.text: Should never be transported by trailer.
Can be an unstable load.
Must be approved by the EPA.

questions.explanation: Drive carefully when transporting hanging meat. This load is unstable because it has a high center of gravity and the meat swinging can affect how you handle the vehicle.
